AfterRoomEntered.maps_to: on_combat_start (oddly_smooth_stone.py:14-17). The sim's Relic base DOES expose a run-level after_room_entered (relics/base.py:194), so the literal mapping existed and was not taken.
AfterRoomEntered.rationale: OddlySmoothStone.cs:21-28 applies PowerVar<DexterityPower>(1m).BaseValue to its owner on AfterRoomEntered when the room `is CombatRoom`; the sim applies the same amount to the same target with the same applier from on_combat_start. This is EXACTLY the mechanism audits/relic/bronze_scales.json and audits/relic/gorget.json already verdicted deliberate-divergence for the identical AfterRoomEntered(CombatRoom) + PowerCmd.Apply body -- one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3, matched and not re-derived. Sequence read rather than assumed: CombatRoom.cs:228 fires Hook.AfterRoomEntered AFTER CombatManager.SetUpCombat and BEFORE AfterCombatRoomLoaded, which then runs AfterCreatureAdded (CombatManager.cs:396), Hook.BeforeCombatStart (:403) and StartTurn (:418) -- so in C# the Dexterity lands one slot earlier than the sim's on_combat_start. AbstractModel.cs:1231-1232 documents AfterRoomEntered+CombatRoom as THE intended slot for 'start of combat effects that should execute before the start of the first turn (like applying powers)'. WHY THIS UNIT NEEDED MORE THAN THE RULE-3 MATCH: Dexterity is not inert like Thorns or Plating -- it MODIFIES block gains (cmds.py:145-147), so any listener in the intervening window that gains powered block would read 1 in the game and 0 in the sim. EXECUTED (py tools/audit/relic_probes_b10.py oddly-smooth-stone): a scan of every ported on_combat_start listener under sts2_rl/relics and sts2_rl/powers.py finds exactly ONE that touches BlockCmd -- PlatingPower._gain_block (powers.py:1058-1061) -- and it is reached from on_combat_start only for the ENEMY side (powers.py:1054-1056) and applied with props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED, so the player's Dexterity cannot reach it. Same observable today; combat start gives powers={'dexterity': 1} and block 0. Rule 7: relics/bronze_scales.py, relics/gorget.py, CombatRoom.cs, CombatManager.cs, AbstractModel.cs, cmds.py, powers.py and relics/base.py are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: `room is CombatRoom` (OddlySmoothStone.cs:23) -- does the sim's on_combat_start fire for exactly the same set of fights?
guards.rationale: Checked because PROMPT.md bug class 20 is about a hook dispatched from the wrong BRANCH. CombatRoom has no subclasses (`grep 'class .*: CombatRoom' src/Core/Rooms/` returns only CombatRoom.cs:23 itself), so Monster, Elite and Boss fights are all CombatRoom and all get the Dexterity, matching the sim's unconditional on_combat_start. The one path worth checking is a combat started FROM an event, because EventRoom.cs:80 fires AfterRoomEntered with an EventRoom (not a CombatRoom): those fights go through EnterCombatWithoutExitingEvent (Events/BattlewornDummy.cs:122), which pushes a real CombatRoom whose own EnterInternal fires AfterRoomEntered again -- so event combats are covered on both sides. Rule 7: CombatRoom.cs, EventRoom.cs and BattlewornDummy.cs are unhashed here.

guards.what: N3: the applier -- `PowerCmd.Apply<DexterityPower>(ctx, Owner.Creature, amount, Owner.Creature, null)` (OddlySmoothStone.cs:26) vs `applier=self.player` (oddly_smooth_stone.py:17)
guards.rationale: Both pass the owner as applier and no cardSource. The trailing `null` is the cardSource, which the sim omits entirely at this call. `new ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext()` is the multiplayer choice context. Rule 7: relics/belt_buckle.py and relics/unsettling_lamp.py are unhashed here.
